passage:
Researchers placed cameras in a forest to study animals at night. The cameras took pictures when they sensed movement.
Students saw photos of deer, wild cats, birds, and animals they had never heard of. The forest seemed empty during the day, but at night it was busy.
The researcher explained that humans often judge nature by what appears in front of them. Cameras can reveal lives that avoid human eyes.
The students became more careful on forest trails. They realized they were visitors in a place full of hidden activity.
A quiet forest is not necessarily an empty forest. It may simply be living on a different schedule.
